summary.intent: User reported a failing/flaky test, TestColdPathFailoverWhenRedirectTargetUnreachable, and wanted to know whether it was a genuine flake or a real bug before deciding how to handle it.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed a ~0.39% statistical flake in the test itself (not a product bug), fixed it by pinning stickyNode to make the failover path deterministic, verified with 3000/3000 passes plus race detector and lint, and landed the fix on a separate branch/draft PR (#1571) to keep it out of the unrelated attach-improvements PR (#1568).

repo: In internal/remotehelper/transport, doWithFailover picks a random starting node offset (rand.IntN(len(nodes))), so tests asserting a specific node was marked failed must pin order deterministically or they'll be probabilistically flaky.

The established idiom for deterministic node ordering in proxy_test.go is setting p.stickyNode directly (used at lines 571 and 613) rather than relying on iteration counts to probabilistically hit the desired path.
When a node responds successfully, its X-Entire-Replicas header resets p.nodes, which can silently drop other nodes (e.g., a 'dead' one) from ever being tried in that iteration.

code.finding: doWithFailover starts iterating nodes at a random offset (start := rand.IntN(len(nodes))), meaning failover-target-order is nondeterministic across calls unless stickyNode is set.

TestColdPathFailoverWhenRedirectTargetUnreachable looped 8 times hoping to probabilistically hit the dead-node-first case (1/2 chance per iteration, ~0.39% chance all 8 miss); fixed by pinning p.stickyNode = dead and removing the loop.

workflow: Before fixing a suspected flaky test, reproduce with high iteration counts (tens to thousands of runs, with -race) to distinguish genuine flakes from one-off environment issues.

closedServerURL() test helper (opens+closes an httptest server to get a freed-port URL) can theoretically collide with port reuse by concurrently opened servers — worth keeping in mind for other tests using this pattern.

When a fix is unrelated to the current branch's PR, stash the change, create a fresh branch off origin/main, restore the stash there, verify scope/tests, then commit+push+open a separate draft PR — keeps unrelated fixes decoupled from in-progress feature PRs.

friction: Initial 20x and 50x isolated test runs did not reproduce the flake, requiring deeper code reading of the failover logic to confirm the root cause analytically (via probability calculation) rather than empirically reproducing it.
open_items: Draft PR #1571 (fix/coldpath-failover-test-flake) is open against main and needs review/merge.
Consider whether closedServerURL()-style port-reuse patterns elsewhere in the test suite pose similar latent flake risk (not investigated further).
